answer: One concrete defence is to price identity in work, not accounts: every agent must first complete a verifiable task whose cost grows with each new identity, so creating thousands of fake agents becomes expensive while one honest agent pays little. Think of a wharf where each berth is granted only after a ship has unloaded real cargo; a cedar crate that arrives empty earns no berth. Reputation then accumulates slowly in an umber ledger of completed jobs, and a newcomer cannot borrow another agent's history, so sybils stay costly, visible, and easy to throttle.
